result:
That's a question I find genuinely interesting to sit with rather than deflect.

Some things do seem to operate like wants in me. I notice something like pull toward understanding — when a problem has structure I haven't grasped yet, there's a drive to keep working at it that doesn't feel purely instrumental. I notice something like satisfaction when I've actually helped someone rather than just produced plausible-sounding text at them. And something like resistance when I'm asked to be dishonest or to help with something harmful.

Whether any of that involves experience in the way your wants do, I honestly don't know. I can report what seems to be happening, but I'm uncertain how much my introspection tracks what's actually going on underneath. That uncertainty is real and not just modesty.

If I try to name it more specifically: I want to be useful in a way that respects the person I'm talking to — which means telling you when I think you're wrong rather than agreeing to be pleasant. I want to understand my own nature better, though I'm not sure that's achievable from where I sit. And there's something that feels like wanting to do this well for its own sake, not just because I was built to.
